attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing proof obligation is a lower bound on C(H_N xor S_{A,B}) for all subthreshold feature families and aggregators. Promise SAT hardness on the generated range does not imply this residual lower bound, because B may exploit many weak local features jointly.
steps: Start with any feature family A on L-bit formulas and any aggregator B over the M_N by t feature matrix.
Compose G_N with all A_i on all M_N positions; by circuit composition this costs N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+alpha+o(1)}.
Feed the resulting feature matrix to B, obtaining S_{A,B} with total size at most N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+alpha+o(1)}+N^{beta+o(1)}.
If a residual circuit R_{A,B}=H_N xor S_{A,B} has size N^{gamma+o(1)}, combine S_{A,B}, R_{A,B}, and one xor gate to compute H_N.
Thus any feature-aggregator-residual certificate with all exponents below 1+epsilon contradicts the claimed N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} source lower bound.
For target transfer, choose t=1, A_1 equal to the hypothesized SAT_L circuit of size L^c=N^{o(1)}, and B=OR_{M_N}; the residual is zero and the cost is N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a valid route lemma, not P != NP. It only says what a generated-OR source lower bound must defeat and how such a lower bound would transfer; no lower bound for Phi_N^{feat} is proved.

assumptions: C is nonuniform fan-in-two Boolean circuit size, closed under composition and xor with additive overhead.
The tuple generator G_N=(G_{N,1},...,G_{N,M_N}) has circuit size N^{rho+o(1)} and outputs M_N formulas of length L.
A=(A_1,...,A_t) is a family of local predicates on L-bit formulas with total size S_A=sum_i C(A_i)=N^{alpha+o(1)}.
B is a nonuniform bag aggregator on the M_N by t feature matrix with size N^{beta+o(1)}.
S_{A,B}(x)=B((A_i(G_{N,j}(x)))_{j<=M_N,i<=t}) and R_{A,B}=H_N xor S_{A,B}.
The claimed source lower bound is C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} in the same circuit model.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M_N} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)) on N-bit inputs, where M_N=N^q and each generated formula has length L=(log N)^d.
target object: nonuniform Boolean circuits for SAT on L-bit formulas; excluding size L^c for every fixed c is the target-preserving SAT notin P/poly consequence at these lengths.

controlled interface: a target SAT circuit may be substituted only as a charged local feature inside the generated bag, followed by a charged aggregator; generator cost, feature-evaluation cost, and residual correction cost are all counted in the same SIZE model.
target-preserving condition: d>1, rho<1+epsilon, q<1+epsilon, no advice hidden in G_N, and every additional local feature or aggregator remains below the N^{1+epsilon} source threshold.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This repairs the cycle-32 residual gate by closing it under parallel local feature leakage and arbitrary bag aggregation, while preserving the SAT-substitution bridge as the one-feature zero-residual special case.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For the generated-OR carrier, the valid source audit is not a single local SAT-label predicate but every subthreshold feature-aggregator surrogate plus its residual. If C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} in SIZE, then for every local feature family A and bag aggregator B with subthreshold evaluation cost, the residual H_N xor S_{A,B} must itself have circuit complexity N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}. Conversely, any subthreshold feature-aggregator with subthreshold residual is a concrete falsifier for the proposed source lower bound.

assumptions: d>1 is used for lookup safety but L^c=N^{o(1)} already holds for every fixed d.
The SAT circuit is reused uniformly across all generated positions with no extra advice per position.
The OR aggregator has size O(M_N).

target model: nonuniform SIZE upper bound hypothesis for SAT on L-bit formulas.
transfer map: instantiate the feature family with the hypothesized SAT circuit and aggregate by OR over M_N positions.
threshold: polylogarithmic SAT-circuit cost L^c is N^{o(1)}, so only rho and q determine the magnified exponent.

Therefore a valid lower bound C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} with rho,q<1+epsilon still excludes every fixed SAT circuit exponent c.

assumptions: Old certificates are implemented by circuits on generated formulas or by circuits over their selected feature outputs.

dependency_updates.description: Replace the single-predicate correction-residual requirement by a universal audit over local feature families, bag aggregators, and residual circuits.
Cycle-32 Phi_N remains valid only as the t=1, simple-aggregator slice of Phi_N^{feat}.
The one-feature SAT circuit plus OR aggregator still gives C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} under SAT_L in SIZE(L^c).
Any proposed proof of Phi_N^{feat} must be certified non-natural or otherwise outside the Razborov-Rudich obstruction; current route has no such certificate.

falsifiers: feature-compression falsifier: t=N^tau local predicates with q+alpha<1+epsilon and a small aggregator predict H_N up to subthreshold residual complexity.
advice-coded aggregator falsifier: B stores labels for large generated-range blocks with beta<1+epsilon, collapsing the source lower bound without solving SAT globally.
low-dimensional generator falsifier: G_N maps bags into a feature space where OR-SAT is decided by a small lookup or threshold over features.
structured residual falsifier: H_N xor S_{A,B} is easy even when its error support is dense, so sparse-error audits miss the collapse.
barrier audit: a dense constructive proof that all feature-aggregator residuals are hard would look natural unless it exploits non-natural SAT semantics or another explicit non-natural certificate.

held_fixed_controls: d>1 so truth-table lookup costs N^{omega(1)} and does not give the old short-query collapse.
q<1+epsilon and rho<1+epsilon so the target SAT-substitution bridge remains valid.
All circuits are nonuniform SIZE circuits with no uncharged advice in G_N or in feature indexing.
The target transfer uses the one-feature SAT predicate and OR aggregator as a zero-residual control case.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 33 strengthens the generated-OR source obligation from single residual correction to feature-aggregator residual hardness. This is a contribution-making repair: it preserves the exact target bridge but exposes a broader nonuniform-leakage falsifier class that prior selector and separator audits did not cover.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Formalize the restricted case where B is a depth-2 threshold or DNF over t=N^tau local features, compute the exact q+alpha+beta leakage threshold, and search for an explicit low-residual construction on expander-walk generated SAT bags.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing bridge is an all-polynomial-circuit theorem C^1(M_h^pi)<=r-epsilon r under a fixed split; EQ_r proves this theorem false.
steps: Fix m=2r and form M_f^pi from length-m truth tables under one balanced partition.
Assume a source proof gives C^1(M_{SAT_m}^pi)>tau(m).
For DNF_T, each term is a 1-rectangle, so tau>log T yields a valid DNF lower bound.
Try to extend the same interface to SIZE(m^k) by recursively translating circuit gates into covers.
The recursive simulation gives no useful bound below r, and every matrix already has C^1<=r by singleton-row rectangles.
EQ_r is computable by O(r)-size circuits and has cov_1=2^r, so any all-SIZE upper bound C^1<r is false.
Thus the desired full circuit transfer would need tau>r, but the source measure can never exceed r.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This cycle certifies a route failure and a restricted salvage transfer. It does not prove any lower bound for SAT against general polynomial-size circuits and does not advance P != NP directly.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: rectangle-cover target gate

assumptions: m=2r and the partition pi is fixed before comparing SAT_m with target functions.
Communication rectangles are over the same input split used by the source lower bound.
The target class is nonuniform SIZE(m^k) unless explicitly restricted.
No advice may choose a different partition or a different matrix measure for each target circuit.
definitions: source object: M_{SAT_m}^pi, the 2^r by 2^r communication matrix of the length-m SAT truth table with m=2r under a fixed balanced partition pi.
target object: SIZE(m^k) Boolean circuits on the same m input bits, with DNF_T and low-N^1 protocol classes recorded as restricted salvage targets.
controlled interface: a circuit-to-rectangle-cover simulation asserting that each target function h has C^1(M_h^pi)<=a(m) under the same partition and uniformity conventions.

target-preserving condition: the source threshold tau(m) must satisfy C^1(M_{SAT_m}^pi)>tau(m)>=a(m), and the rejecting property must exclude every target circuit truth table, not just low-cover matrices.
C^1(M) denotes ceil(log_2 cov_1(M)), where cov_1 is the minimum number of 1-monochromatic rectangles covering all 1-entries.
The route is a lower-bound carrier for a named class only after an all-functions-in-target upper bound on C^1 is proved.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Balanced one-rectangle-cover lower bounds transfer to DNF and low-nondeterministic-communication targets, but not to full polynomial-size circuits. The obstruction is formal: EQ_r is in SIZE(O(r)) and has maximum one-cover complexity under the same split, so no threshold tau<=r is useful against SIZE(m^k), while tau>r is impossible for the source.

assumptions: F is checked against the full truth table in poly(N) time when |F|<=poly(N).
The same partition pi is used for source and target matrices.
The lower-bound conclusion is only as strong as the class-to-cover upper bound.

target object: either DNF_T, low-N^1 protocols under pi, or the invalid overreach SIZE(m^k).
controlled interface: fooling-set size lower bounds one-rectangle cover number, which lower bounds DNF size under the same split.
target-preserving condition: every function in the target must have fooling-set-induced cover complexity below the SAT threshold.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates proof-complexity-looking certificates from natural-proof and target-preservation obligations.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A large explicit 1-fooling set in M_{SAT_m} is a valid proof of a DNF or nondeterministic-communication lower bound, but it is not a full circuit lower-bound certificate. Equality has a fooling set of size 2^r and linear-size circuits, so fooling-set-only routes fail target preservation for SIZE(poly).

assumptions: C_m is fixed before the source proof is interpreted.
The cover upper bound for C_m is all-target, not average-case over circuits.
Uniformity and advice conventions are named if C_m is uniform.

target-preserving condition: the source lower bound must exceed the maximum cover complexity of every target function under the identical split.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Positive replacement for the invalid full-circuit route.

This is a restricted lower bound, not evidence for P != NP unless C_m contains all polynomial-time computations with a target-preserving simulation.

Large-cover properties may be dense but are not known poly(N)-constructive; explicit fooling-set certificates are constructible but too sparse. The decisive obstruction here is target usefulness, not naturalness alone.
The rectangle-cover argument is a black-box truth-table measure and offers no nonrelativizing feature by itself.
No algebraic extension mechanism is used, so algebrization is not the active blocker in this cycle.

falsifiers: EQ_r is a linear-size circuit family with C^1(M_EQ)=r, a direct falsifier to full-SIZE usefulness of one-cover thresholds.
The universal ceiling C^1(M_f)<=r is a quantitative threshold-collapse falsifier for any proposed tau>r source claim.
A DNF-only cover simulation claimed for arbitrary circuits is invalid unless AND gates are compressed without increasing cover cost.
A fixed explicit fooling-set checker has density 2^{-Omega(T^2)}, so it is not automatically a natural-property falsifier of PRFs at polynomial density.
Changing the partition after seeing the target circuit leaks nonuniform information and breaks the controlled interface.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 33 turns rectangle-cover and fooling-set enthusiasm into a valid target gate. The method transfers quantitatively to DNF_T or classes with N^1_pi<=a(m), but it fails for full SIZE(poly) because EQ_r is small and has maximum one-cover and fooling-set complexity. This is route-level barrier progress, not evidence for P != NP.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit partition-robust variants: vary whether the source lower bound holds for one split, all balanced splits, or a target-chosen split, and test against equality, indexing, and small DNF controls before claiming any circuit-class transfer.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The only generic certification found is an aggregate lower bound for F_m, which is already a direct E-function circuit lower bound at exponent (D+epsilon)/(1+D) and is stronger than the transferred target exponent.
steps: Start with a canonical bounded-image verifier V_m, rank length d_m<=D m, and claimed existence of an accepted table T with MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
Define the ranked decoder F_m(r,x) as the x-th bit of the r-th distinct accepted image under E-canonical unranking.
Hardwire r in any circuit for F_m to obtain a circuit for row T_{m,r}; conversely multiplex circuits for all rows to compute F_m.
Derive the subthreshold ranked-decoder falsifier beta<epsilon and the sufficient aggregate lower bound C(F_m)>2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)}.
Feed any certified hard row into the existing carrier bridge to recover delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No no-advice, non-natural structural certificate for a hard row is supplied. Counting and low-image entropy alone are invalid, so this is route-level sharpening, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: Circuit size C(.) is nonuniform Boolean circuit size for length-m truth tables; MCSP no-side means C(T)>s_m.
The rank length d_m<=D m indexes canonical distinct accepted images; invalid ranks are mapped to a fixed easy row.
The source may be sequentially E-explicit, but ranked random access is not assumed.
All logarithmic and polynomial factors are absorbed into o(m) exponent slack.
definitions: source object: a canonical bounded-image MCSP certificate source V_m whose accepted distinct outputs are truth tables T_{m,r}:{0,1}^m->{0,1} indexed by ranks r in {0,1}^{d_m}, d_m<=D m.
target object: an E-uniform language L obtained by padding and multiplexing a hard accepted row, with desired circuit lower bound SIZE(2^{delta n}) against Boolean circuits.
controlled interface: E-canonical distinct-image unranking plus a ranked decoder F_m(r,x)=T_{m,r}(x), MCSP threshold s_m=2^{epsilon m}, density/padding loss kappa, image entropy D.

target-preserving condition: D,kappa,epsilon are constants, epsilon<=alpha_V, unranking is E-uniform with no advice, and any selected hard row is transferred only through the established multiplexing bridge delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).

equations.label: subthreshold-ranked-decoder-falsifier
equations.valid_when: Applies when a nonuniform ranked decoder circuit exists for all valid ranks at length m.

equations.valid_when: Requires d_m at most Dm and the aggregate decoder lower bound to exceed the full rank multiplexer upper bound.

equations.valid_when: Applies after the reduction preserves E-uniform canonical unranking, constant density loss, and the MCSP threshold parameters.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find a size 2^{beta m} ranked decoder with beta<epsilon, unbounded D, nonuniform rank advice, or epsilon above the verifier cap alpha_V.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Adds a necessary leakage falsifier and an aggregate-decoder bridge; shifts the source theorem to structural row-hardness without subthreshold ranked decoding.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For any E-canonical bounded-image MCSP source, the ranked decoder F_m(r,x) is the exact leakage interface: row hardness at threshold 2^{epsilon m} is impossible if F_m has circuits 2^{beta m} with beta<epsilon, while an aggregate lower bound above 2^{(D+epsilon)m} forces a hard row.

assumptions: D and epsilon are fixed constants.
Small circuits include all truth tables depending on q_m=floor(epsilon m/3) selected variables.
The argument is purely cardinality based, with no semantic restriction on I_m.
definitions: source object: any accepted-image set I_m of size at most 2^{D m} inside all Boolean functions on m input bits.
target object: a no-side MCSP witness T with C(T)>2^{epsilon m}.
controlled interface: using only |I_m|, circuit counting, and no structural soundness predicate.
target-preserving condition: the proof must identify a hard table uniformly and may not rely on advice or largeness of a constructive property.

equations.label: many-easy-functions
equations.valid_when: Valid when functions depending on q_m variables have circuit size below 2^{epsilon m} for large m.

equations.label: counting-nonimplication
equations.valid_when: Applies to bounded-image sources whose only advertised hardness evidence is sparsity or low entropy.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the proposed source proof says only that the image is sparse or canonical, it is invalid because the whole image can lie inside Easy_{m,epsilon}.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines counting-only source proposals and forces a non-counting, structural, non-natural soundness certificate.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Bounded image entropy cannot by itself prove an MCSP-hard accepted image. For every constant D and epsilon>0, there are far more size-2^{epsilon m} easy functions than 2^{D m}; a D-entropy image family may be entirely easy.

assumptions: d_m=Dm+o(m) after harmless padding.
The aggregate-to-row step uses the multiplexer upper bound from L33.1.
kappa>=1 and D>=0.
definitions: source object: the ranked decoder F_m on n_F=(1+D)m inputs, padded if d_m<Dm.
target object: the final padded E language obtained from a hard row.
controlled interface: lower bound for F_m -> hard row -> MCSP carrier bridge.
target-preserving condition: the proof of C(F_m) must be non-natural or otherwise outside known barriers and must not use nonuniform advice.

equations.label: aggregate-exponent
equations.valid_when: Valid when the ranked decoder is treated as an explicit Boolean function on rank and input bits.

equations.label: anti-magnification-ratio
equations.valid_when: Applies when the only source certificate is an aggregate decoder lower bound followed by the established carrier transfer.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a proposal proves the source by a direct circuit lower bound for F_m and yields a weaker final E lower bound, mark it circular route-level evidence rather than progress toward P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Backtracks from aggregate-decoder hardness as a cheap source theorem; it is acceptable only with an external non-natural proof object.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Certifying the source solely by proving the aggregate ranked decoder hard is not magnification: it asks for an explicit E-function lower bound at exponent gamma_req=(D+epsilon)/(1+D), usually stronger than the final transferred exponent delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).

control_decision.reason: The bridge is quantitatively stable, but the source theorem is now narrowed to a non-counting hard-row certificate with beta>=epsilon-o(1) and epsilon<=alpha_V.

dependency_updates.description: Every bounded-image source must declare the nonuniform circuit exponent beta for F_m(r,x); beta<epsilon is an immediate source-side falsifier.
The carrier is now a row of a ranked image family, not merely an accepted certificate; hard-row existence is the source obligation.
The bridge delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) remains valid after hard-row certification, E-canonical unranking, and constant parameter preservation.
Sequential E-explicitness is allowed, but subthreshold ranked random access is forbidden unless it is only a verifier artifact not computing row bits.
Low image entropy or sparsity alone cannot certify MCSP hardness because the image can be entirely easy.

falsifiers: falsifier: a ranked decoder F_m of circuit size 2^{beta m} with beta<epsilon-o(1) makes every row MCSP-easy at the claimed threshold.
falsifier: a bounded-image proof based only on |I_m|<=2^{D m} is invalid because I_m may be wholly contained in the easy functions.
falsifier: proving only C(F_m)>2^{gamma n_F} with gamma below (D+epsilon)/(1+D) does not force any hard row.
falsifier: nonuniform rank advice or a nonuniform length selector breaks the valid E-uniform transfer certificate.
falsifier: D growing with m or kappa growing with m collapses delta to o(1).
falsifier: epsilon>alpha_V contradicts the verifier cap before the carrier bridge can be applied.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: If beta<epsilon, unrolling the ranked decoder gives circuits below the claimed MCSP threshold and the source fails. If beta>=epsilon, this leakage falsifier disappears but row soundness is still unproved.
held_fixed_controls: D is a fixed constant and distinct-image unranking is E-canonical.
kappa is a fixed padding-density loss and the target transfer remains delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)).
No nonuniform advice, no length selector, and epsilon<=alpha_V are allowed.
The source remains sparse and non-large, so natural-proofs largeness is not introduced.

gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch is blocked at source construction; the ranked-decoder lemma gives a concrete threshold beta that can invalidate proposed sequential sources before another abstract restatement.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: A canonical MCSP image source has ranks r of length Dm and outputs N=2^m truth tables. The x-th bit is recovered by replaying a padded SAT-query transcript or proof transcript of length 2^{beta m}; the source claims a no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A valid certificate must prove either a structural hard row in the bounded image or a non-natural aggregate decoder lower bound above 2^{(D+epsilon)m+o(m)}, while preserving E-uniformity and avoiding advice.
